Today in music class I dedicated a song to 'a person in this room who knows who she is'. Everyone laughed and looked around. Dolma looked at her desk. Her face went a bit pink, or maybe that was the light. I don't know what it meant. After class Sahil, my friend, said I'd been too obvious, and I said I was only joking.

On the last evening before Varun left for college in Pune, the village fair was lit with strings of bulbs. Ira walked beside him past the bangle stalls, eating a paper cone of roasted chana.
"So you'll forget all of us in a month," she said, laughing. "Especially me."
Varun laughed too. "Maybe. You'll be too busy with your exams."
Ira kept her eyes on the chana. "Maybe I'll miss you. A little. Like, a small amount."
Varun stopped by the giant wheel. He had always walked her home when the lights went out, and had shared his old notes without her asking.
"Ira. Are you joking, or are you saying something?"
She took a breath. "Saying something. Half."
"I'll miss you too," he said. "More than a small amount."
They didn't say anything else. They just bought one more cone of chana and shared it.

On a bench outside their school in Porto, Vera had been rehearsing the sentence for two days.
"Hypothetically," she said to Camila, "if someone had feelings for a girl in our year, would people be weird about it?"
She said it lightly, peeling her orange, not looking up.
Camila was quiet for a moment. She had always been the one who shut down jokes about other people's crushes, and who kept Vera's secrets without ever being asked.
"Some people might be," Camila said. "I wouldn't. Is this hypothetical-hypothetical, or you-hypothetical?"
Vera laughed nervously and almost said "joking." Instead she said, "Me. I think. It's new."
Camila bumped her shoulder. "Thank you for telling me. You can tell me more whenever. Or never."
Vera let out a breath she didn't know she'd been holding, and handed Camila half the orange.

qa.a: On a bench outside their school in Porto.

qa.a: Vera was nervous and afraid of the reaction, peeling the orange and not looking up while testing the response.
